prompt: Write one generic recursive fold over a binary tree of ints, then derive total, leafCount, depth and render from it without writing recursion a second time.
explanation: A fold (catamorphism) captures the shape of the recursion once: one function says what a leaf becomes, another says how two folded sub-results are joined, and the traversal itself is written a single time. Because the result type R is generic, the same fold yields an int sum, an int depth, or a String rendering -- only the two functions change. Note how depth differs from total purely in its branch function, 1 + Math.max(a, b) instead of a + b, which is the whole point of separating traversal from the operation.
hints: The leaf case ends the recursion: if (node instanceof NumberLeaf leaf) return onLeaf.apply(leaf.value());
For a SumBranch, fold the left and the right sub-trees first, then pass both results to onBranch.apply(...).
leafCount ignores the leaf value entirely (value -> 1) and adds on branches; depth uses the same leaf function but 1 + Math.max(a, b) on branches.
